primary_meaning: Gentile believers being incorporated (as wild olive branches) into the cultivated olive tree representing the covenant people of God / Israel, thereby sharing in the root and rich sap of the Abrahamic promises and blessings while some natural branches are broken off for unbelief (with the possibility of re-grafting).

alternatives.meaning: Supersessionist reading in which the olive tree is identified primarily with the Church that replaces ethnic Israel, so that Gentiles constitute the new permanent people of God.
basis: Romans 11:17-24 (read as permanent displacement of the natural branches)

alternatives.meaning: Emphasis on the temporary nature of Jewish unbelief and the future mass re-grafting of ethnic Israel into their own olive tree, with Gentiles as co-participants rather than replacements.
Personal/spiritual application to individual believers’ vital union with Christ or the source of spiritual life, sometimes conflated with the vine-and-branches imagery.

notes: The grafting metaphor is almost exclusively derived from Paul’s explicit olive-tree allegory in Romans 11 and is one of the most consistently recognized New Testament symbols for the relationship between Israel and Gentile believers / the Church. Variations concern ecclesiological implications (inclusion vs. replacement, present vs. future status of Israel) rather than the core agricultural image itself.
